In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many factors, both environmental and genetic, that are associated with the risk of developing breast cancer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most significant risk factors for breast cancer are early age of menarche, late age of menopause, nulliparity, late age at first full-term pregnancy, and high parity, all of which are related to a longer period of exposure to estrogen.
the most important risk factor for breast cancer in women is a family history of the disease.
there is a need for more prospective studies and more studies on dietary factors, particularly on the role of phytoestrogens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
breast cancer is not only a disease of the Western world but that it is a disease of affluent societies.
there are many factors that contribute to the development of breast cancer, and that there is a need to understand the complex interplay between these factors in the development of this disease.
